paragraphs: A Map of Our Town, drawn by Leo and Mia. Teacher Kim asked us to make a map for visitors. Everybody in the club helped, and Lily checked the words. The map shows five important places in our town. We used a ruler and five color pens, and the drawing took two club hours. Look at the key under the map to find them.

The key uses a color and a shape for each place. A red square is the train station. An orange circle is the market. A blue star is the town library. A green triangle is the science museum. A yellow flag is our school.

The station is at the top left of the map, and the market is at the top right. A big road goes from the station to the market. Two bus stops are on the big road, but they are not on the map. The library is in the middle of the map, below the big road. Our school is at the bottom left, and the museum is at the bottom right. Maybe you want to walk from the school to the library. It takes ten minutes.

The train station is open all day, and you can buy a ticket at the desk. The market opens at six o'clock in the morning and closes at noon. It is crowded at eight o'clock, because many people buy fruit and flowers. The walk from the station to the market takes fifteen minutes along the big road. Ask a seller for directions if you cannot find the way. A woman at the market helped us to find the right road.

The town library has a quiet room with computers. Children can use them for surfing the web for one hour. You can contact the library desk by email. The library is open from nine o'clock to five o'clock. The science museum is at the bottom right of the map. It has a free activity for children every Saturday morning. Guide Ann gives advice about the best time to visit. She answers every email from visitors.
Our advice is simple: walk, or take the bus. Maybe the map is not perfect, but it helps everybody to find the way. Do you want to see another place on the map? Tell Leo and Mia in a comment!
